comparator.name: Bachelor Sociologie
comparator.academicYear: 2025-2026 (current official Onderwijs- en Examenregeling; independently corroborated by the current official programme webpages checked 2026-09-27 for the Fall-2026 entrant cohort, since VU had not yet published a distinct 2026-2027 OER for Sociologie via the study guide at time of check)
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from VU Amsterdam's current official sources for the Fall-2026 cohort: the current Dutch-language 'Bachelor Sociologie' overview, 'Inhoud' (content) and 'Toekomst' (career) pages (all checked 2026-09-27), and the 2025-2026 Onderwijs- en Examenregeling (OER), the most recent formally adopted Sociologie OER publicly available at time of check (VU had not yet published a distinct 2026-2027 OER for this programme via the study guide). The current live 'Inhoud' page reproduces, unit for unit, the same year-1/year-2/year-3 curriculum the 2025-2026 OER's Bijlage III jaarschema sets out (Maatschappelijke vraagstukken en interventies, Diversiteit in een democratische context, Project 1: Beleidsinterventie, Project 2: Opdrachtonderzoek, Sociale ongelijkheid 1 & 2, Big Data en Computational Thinking, Individuen sociale netwerken en technologie, Media macht en technologie, Netwerk- en social media analyse, Interpretatief onderzoek, Co-creatief onderzoek, Project 3: Sociaal ondernemerschap, Project 4: Consultancy, Onderzoek naar effecten van interventies, Wetenschapsfilosofie, Bachelorthesisproject Sociologie), so the 2025-2026 OER is used as the controlling source for the compulsory-unit table, cross-verified against the current official page content for the applicable Fall-2026 entrant cohort per Section 2.1. Article 10.2 (Opleidingstrajecten en/of afstudeerrichtingen) states 'Niet van toepassing': the normalized target cp-000117 (registry row 118, source_provider_id 111A136, recognized_programme_code 56601, programme_unit_code 1001O5925, languages_json=["NLD"]) is the generic Dutch-taught Bachelor Sociologie with no formal afstudeerrichting to instantiate, so routeSelection is null. Article 2.1.3 fixes every onderwijseenheid at 6 EC or a multiple thereof. Bijlage III's Year 1 (60 EC) comprises ten 6-EC units: Maatschappelijke vraagstukken en interventies (S_MVI, niveau 100), Diversiteit in een democratische context (S_DDC, 100), Identiteit, diversiteit en inclusie (S_IDIS, 200), Methodologie van sociaalwetenschappelijk onderzoek (S_MTSWO, 100), Project 1: Beleidsinterventie (S_P1B, 200; Article 10.4.6 folds the diagnostic taaltoets into this unit's grade), Sociale ongelijkheid 1: onderwijs, arbeidsmarkt en inkomen (S_SO1OAI, 100), Beschrijvende en inferentiële statistiek (S_BIS, 100), Sociale ongelijkheid 2: Gezondheid en de verzorgingsstaat (S_SO2GV, 200), Geschiedenis van de sociale wetenschappen (S_GSW, 200, part of the Article 11.1 academische kern) and Project 2: Opdrachtonderzoek (S_P2P, 200); the zero-EC Mentoraat Sociologie eerste jaar (S_MS1) carries no separate credit and is not encoded as its own component. Year 2 (60 EC) comprises ten further 6-EC units: Individuen, sociale netwerken en technologie (S_ISNT, 300), Big Data en Computational Thinking (S_BDCT, 200), Netwerk- en social media analyse (S_NSMA, 300), Media, macht en technologie (S_MMT, 300), Project 3: Sociaal ondernemerschap (S_P3SO, 300), Interpretatief onderzoek (S_IOZ, 200), one restricted 300-level choice from Beyond Gender Inequalities / Confronting Commodity Chains / Towards Better Care and Welfare, Co-creatief onderzoek (S_CCO, 200), one restricted 300-level choice from AI & Society: Fixing Algorithmic Decision Making / Improving a Sustainable World by Social Entrepreneurship / The Human Dimension of Sustainable Development, and Project 4: Consultancy (S_P4C, 300); the zero-EC Mentoraat Sociologie tweede jaar (S_MS2) again carries no separate credit. No official source names target-specific evidence favouring one option within either restricted three-way choice, but registry programme-interest evidence for this exact target independently corroborates two specific selections without changing the credit total: row 5349 ('gender and society', Curricular topic) supports selecting Beyond Gender Inequalities (S_BGI), and row 5345 ('how algorithms shape polarisation', Direct programme interest) supports selecting AI & Society: Fixing Algorithmic Decision Making (S_AIS); both are also the first-listed option in the official jaarschema, independently satisfying the neutral official-order tie-break under Section 2.1 even without that evidence. Year 3 (60 EC): Article 12.1 fixes a genuine 30-EC vrije keuzeruimte in the first semester, filled by a programmed minor (Article 12.2 lists Anthropology, Bestuurswetenschap, Communicatiewetenschap, Communication Science, Organisatiewetenschap, Educatieve minor Maatschappijleer, or the 30-EC national Climate Sociology minor, none requiring examination-board approval), a free choice of units (at least 12 EC at level 300), or a stage; no target-specific evidence favours one minor, so -- consistent with Section 2.1's instruction to preserve genuine open elective or profiling space explicitly rather than inventing content for it -- this 30-EC space is recorded as a single generic keuzeruimte component. The second semester adds Onderzoek naar effecten van interventies (S_OEI, 300, 6 EC; Article 9.1 requires Beschrijvende en inferentiële statistiek, Sociale ongelijkheid 2 and Interpretatief onderzoek first), Wetenschapsfilosofie (S_WF, 300 per the Bijlage III jaarschema; Article 11.1 lists it as niveau 200 in the academische kern definition, a minor label discrepancy between the two OER sections that does not affect its EC or compulsory status) and Bachelorthesisproject Sociologie (S_BTPS, 18 EC, 300; Article 9.1 admits students only after 90 EC of the Year 1-2 units and Onderzoek naar effecten van interventies are passed). 60 (Year 1) + 60 (Year 2) + 60 (Year 3: 30 keuzeruimte + 6 + 6 + 18) = 180 EC. Article 10.1's doelstelling and Article 10.3's eindtermen independently corroborate this reconstruction, naming 'sociologie en aangrenzende disciplines' (sociology and adjacent disciplines), diversity/inequality/'communicatie & technologie' (KI2) as the programme's three headline knowledge domains, quantitative-and-qualitative research training (KI4), and designing, implementing and evaluating interventions for a societal partner (T4-T5) as the programme's own defining learning outcomes -- independently corroborated by the current official Toekomst page naming beleidsadviseur, onderzoeker, sociaal ondernemer and consultant as its four named professional outcomes and Article 9.1's confirmation that these four roles are practised through the four named compulsory project courses. No further official source needed to be consulted: the current official overview/content/career pages and the 2025-2026 OER together establish a complete, internally consistent, entirely accounted-for 180-EC pathway with explicit EC and niveau for every compulsory unit, an explicit basis for both restricted elective selections, and an explicit, UCR-independent judgment (preserving rather than instantiating the free keuzeruimte) fixed before any UCR course was considered.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: General sociological theory and the transdisciplinary combination of sociology with adjacent social sciences
Social inequality and unequal opportunities in education, work, health and politics
Diversity, identity and inclusion in a democratic context
Survey research, descriptive/inferential statistics and quantitative social-scientific methodology
Qualitative interviews, interpretive research and participatory/co-creative research with societal partners
Designing and evaluating social interventions and translating sociological evidence into practical solutions
Independent sociological research culminating in the bachelor thesis
Historical and philosophical foundations of social-scientific knowledge
adjacent: Digitalisation and social change: social media, algorithms, big data, social-network analysis and the power of media/technology companies
Applied professional practice: policy analysis and advice, commissioned social research, social entrepreneurship and consultancy
questions: Illustrative or temporary applied research topics used in the programme's project courses with external partners (the social side of the energy transition, educational inequality in mixed schools, discrimination in internships, researching interventions for the municipality of Amsterdam)

Graduate career and further-study trajectories the programme prepares students for (policy adviser, researcher, social entrepreneur, consultant, consultancy careers, and further study in Social Sciences for a Digital Society or teaching)

alternatives.label: Sociology, Inequality and Applied Social Research
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by UCR's own Sociology unit (5 of 24: Introduction to Sociology, Modern Sociology, Qualitative Research Methodology, Social Movements & Environmental Justice, New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory), reinforced by a quantitative-methods cluster (3 of 24: Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Econometrics) and a policy-advice/consultancy-adjacent applied cluster (5 of 24: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Public Economics, Law, Society & Justice, Rhetoric in Action, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership), with the remaining courses (Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Social Psychology, Introduction to Economics, Modern History, Introduction to Political Philosophy, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Leadership & Diversity Management, Histories of Gender, Introduction to Data Science) providing the transdisciplinary and diversity/inequality breadth the comparator's own doelstelling and eindtermen (KI1-KI2) name as defining the field. The label names sociology first for the dominant disciplinary anchor, inequality second for the diversity/inequality cluster that runs through the first year, and applied social research third for the methods-plus-policy-advice backbone that mirrors the comparator's own four-professional-role project structure at a general, non-specialised level.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to VU's generalist Bachelor Sociologie (Article 10.2 confirms no formal afstudeerrichtingen exist for this normalized target): a general-sociology core -- introductory and advanced sociological theory, social inequality, diversity/identity/inclusion, and quantitative, qualitative and participatory research methods -- combined with UCR's political-science, history, philosophy, economics and psychology offerings to reproduce the programme's own transdisciplinary combination of sociology with adjacent social sciences, and with a light applied/policy-advice thread (negotiation, public economics, law/society/justice, persuasive communication) reflecting the programme's own general orientation toward translating sociological evidence into practical solutions, while leaving the 30-EC vrije keuzeruimte honestly preserved as unclaimed elective space and several specialist components (health/welfare-state inequality, dedicated network/social-media analysis, co-creative research, and the impact-evaluation and philosophy-of-science components) genuinely unmatched.
progression: BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes BENLEAD211, BENECON312 (semester 6), BENLEAD312, BENECON311 (semester 4) and BENLEAD311 (semester 5), which formally require it. HCBGATE102 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precedes HCBPSYC314 (semester 4), which formally requires it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Introductory gateway and level-1 courses (Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Introduction to Sociology, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Research Methods & Statistics, Histories of Gender, Social Psychology) are concentrated in semesters 1-2, and level-3 advanced work (New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory, Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Public Economics, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Econometrics) is concentrated in semesters 3-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced applied work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternatives.label: Sociology of the Digital Society: Media, Data and Algorithmic Power
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum retains UCR's Sociology theory/methods anchor (5 of 24: Introduction to Sociology, Modern Sociology, Qualitative Research Methodology, Social Movements & Environmental Justice, New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory) and quantitative-methods anchor (3 of 24: Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Econometrics), but replaces the closest match's political-science/history/philosophy/psychology/applied-policy breadth with a deep data-science, artificial-intelligence and media/communication cluster (9 of 24: Mathematical Methods, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Database Management Systems, The Art of Rhetorical Communication, Persuasive Communication, Media & Race, Rhetoric in Action), plus Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Youth Resilience to Extremism, Introduction to Economics, Law Society & Justice, Foundations of Comparative Politics and Social Psychology. The label names sociology of the digital society first because every scheduled course studies society through, or is applied to, digital technology, and media, data and algorithmic power second for the three concrete strands (media/communication, data/AI, and algorithmic decision-making) that organise the alternative's distinctive academic priorities.
alternatives.concept: A genuinely different second UCR route evidenced by five Direct-programme-interest rows that specifically name digitalisation and social change (5329), why young people feel lonely in a connected world (5326), how social media affects loneliness (5344), how algorithms shape polarisation (5345) and privacy and the power of technology companies (5347) as recurring foci of the current programme, corroborated by three Curricular-topic support rows (big-data and computational social research 5333, social-network and social-media analysis 5336, media power and public debate 5346) and independently confirmed by the current official Inhoud page's own compulsory second-year curriculum (Big Data en Computational Thinking, Individuen sociale netwerken en technologie, Netwerk- en social media analyse, Media macht en technologie) and by the OER's own KI2 eindterm naming 'communicatie & technologie' as one of the programme's three headline knowledge domains: a concentration retaining the same shared sociological-theory and methods core but replacing the closest match's diversity-management, negotiation, public-economics and transdisciplinary-breadth cluster with UCR's full available data-science, artificial-intelligence, database and media/communication offerings, studying how digital technology, algorithms and media power reshape social connection, polarisation and privacy.
progression: BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes BENECON312 (semester 6), which formally requires it. DISGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes DISDATA311 (semester 4), which formally requires it. BENENTR211 (semester 4, formally requiring BENGATE102) is scheduled after BENGATE102 (semester 2). Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Introductory gateway and level-1/level-2 courses (Introduction to Sociology, Law Society & Justice, Foundations of Comparative Politics, The Art of Rhetorical Communication, Mathematical Methods, Qualitative Research Methodology) are concentrated in semesters 1-2, and level-3 advanced work (New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Persuasive Communication, Media & Race, Youth Resilience to Extremism, Econometrics) is concentrated in semesters 3-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced technical and applied work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.
alternatives.distinctness: VU's Bachelor Sociologie names digitalisation, social media, algorithms and privacy as recurring compulsory second-year content (Big Data en Computational Thinking, Individuen sociale netwerken en technologie, Netwerk- en social media analyse, Media macht en technologie) and as five of its own generator-eligible programme-interest rows (5326, 5329, 5344, 5345, 5347), independently corroborated by curricular-topic support rows on big data, network analysis and media power (5333, 5336, 5346) and by the OER's own KI2 eindterm naming diversity, inequality and 'communicatie & technologie' as the programme's three headline knowledge domains. The closest match reproduces the shared sociological-theory and methods core together with UCR's political-science, history, philosophy and applied-policy breadth. This alternative instead retains the identical GOSSOCI theory anchor (GOSSOCI111, 212, 214, 215, 311) and quantitative-methods anchor (BENGATE102, HCBPSYC211, BENECON312) -- 8 of 24 courses shared with the closest match beyond Personal & Professional Development -- but replaces 9 of the closest match's remaining courses with UCR's Mathematical Methods, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Database Management Systems, three media/communication courses, a youth-extremism/technology psychology course and a marketing course, for a total of nine data-science/AI/media courses concentrating the programme on the sociology of digital technology and its power. This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from a generalist sociology-of-inequality-and-diversity programme to a single-domain digital-society concentration, and the two alternatives share 15 of 24 courses while differing in 9 of 24 each way (67.5 EC), comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum.

alternatives.label: Sociology, Social Entrepreneurship and Consultancy Practice
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum retains UCR's Sociology theory/methods anchor (4 of 24: Introduction to Sociology, Modern Sociology, Qualitative Research Methodology, New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory) and a core-methods pair (Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods), but replaces the closest match's political-science/history/philosophy/psychology/diversity-management breadth with UCR's full available entrepreneurship, marketing, strategy, finance and leadership offerings (11 of 24: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Market Research, Strategy & Digital Transformation, Consumer Product Design, International Business & Governance, Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Money Banking & Finance, Accounting & Corporate Finance, Personal Leadership, Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Leadership Communication), plus Public Economics, Law Society & Justice, Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, Social Psychology, Introduction to Economics and Rhetoric in Action. The label names sociology first for the retained disciplinary anchor, social entrepreneurship second for the dominant venture-creation cluster, and consultancy practice third for the strategy/negotiation/finance/leadership cluster that together organise this alternative's distinctive academic priorities.
alternatives.concept: A genuinely different third UCR route evidenced by four Stable-study-direction rows that specifically name policy analysis and advice (5338), commissioned social research (5339), social entrepreneurship (5340) and consulting on social challenges (5341) as recurring, structurally embedded professional roles of the current programme, independently confirmed by the current official Inhoud page's own statement that the programme's four project courses train students in exactly these four professional roles -- beleidsmedewerker, onderzoeker, sociaal ondernemer, consultant -- through Project 1: Beleidsinterventie, Project 2: Opdrachtonderzoek, Project 3: Sociaal ondernemerschap and Project 4: Consultancy: a concentration retaining the same shared sociological-theory and methods core but replacing the closest match's transdisciplinary political-science/history/philosophy/psychology breadth with UCR's full available entrepreneurship, marketing, strategy, finance and leadership offerings, studying how sociological evidence is translated into venture-creation, commissioned research, policy advice and consultancy practice for real organisations.
progression: BENGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) is a formal prerequisite for Strategy & Digital Transformation, Market Research, International Business & Governance and Money Banking & Finance, and is scheduled in semester 1, before every course that depends on it. BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Public Economics (semester 4) and Marketing & Consumer Engagement (semester 6), which formally require it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Introductory gateway and level-1 courses (Introduction to Sociology, Law Society & Justice, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Personal Leadership) are concentrated in semesters 1-3, and level-3 advanced work (New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory, Market Research, Money Banking & Finance, Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Public Economics, International Business & Governance) is concentrated in semesters 2-5, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced applied work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.
alternatives.distinctness: VU's Bachelor Sociologie structurally organises its entire first two years around four named professional roles -- policy adviser, researcher, social entrepreneur and consultant -- realised through four dedicated compulsory project courses, and independently names these same four roles as generator-eligible Stable-study-direction programme-interest rows (5338, 5339, 5340, 5341) rather than merely as career outcomes. The closest match already includes a light applied-policy thread (Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Public Economics, Law Society & Justice, Rhetoric in Action, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership -- 5 of 24 courses) reflecting the programme's general orientation toward practical solutions, but this alternative goes materially further: it retains the identical GOSSOCI theory anchor (GOSSOCI111, 212, 214, 311; Social Movements & Environmental Justice is dropped) and core-methods pair (BENGATE102, HCBPSYC211) -- 7 of 24 courses shared with the closest match beyond Personal & Professional Development -- but replaces 11 of the closest match's remaining courses (Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Histories of Gender, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Modern History, Introduction to Political Philosophy, Leadership & Diversity Management, Social Movements & Environmental Justice, Econometrics, Introduction to Data Science, Rhetoric in Action's original policy framing) with UCR's Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, four further Entrepreneurship-track courses, three Leadership-track courses, two Finance-track courses and a Human Rights Law & Philosophy course, for a total of eleven business/entrepreneurship/leadership courses concentrating the programme on the translation of sociological evidence into professional practice. This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from a generalist sociology-with-political-science-and-psychology programme to a single-domain applied-practice concentration organised around venture creation, commissioned research, policy advice and consultancy, and the alternative differs from the closest match in 11 of 24 courses each way (82.5 EC) and from the digital-society alternative in 12 of 24 courses each way (90 EC), comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum in both comparisons.

selection.assessment: The closest match directly owns ten generator-eligible rows: why parental social status shapes children's opportunities (5325); social inequality (5327); diversity, identity and inclusion (5328); finding practical solutions to social problems (5330); combining sociology with other social sciences (5331); survey research and statistical analysis (5332); qualitative interviews and interpretive research (5334); participatory and co-creative research (5335); designing and evaluating social interventions (5337); and sociological research (5354), all of which describe the programme's own general sociological core, methods pluralism and applied orientation rather than an independent substantive direction, and are therefore substantively covered by the closest match's own core concept rather than forced into a residual candidate. The remaining nine generator-eligible rows were independently assessed as two coherent candidate directions: 'Sociology of the Digital Society: Media, Data and Algorithmic Power' (5326, 5329, 5344, 5345, 5347), additionally supported by curricular-topic evidence on big data, network analysis and media power (5333, 5336, 5346) and independently corroborated by the current official Inhoud page's own compulsory second-year digital-society curriculum and by the OER's KI2 eindterm naming communicatie & technologie as one of the programme's three headline knowledge domains; and 'Sociology, Social Entrepreneurship and Consultancy Practice' (5338, 5339, 5340, 5341), independently corroborated by the current official Inhoud page's own statement that the programme's four compulsory project courses structurally train students in exactly these four professional roles. Both candidates pass all four gates: each is evidence-backed by generator-eligible rows the programme's own current official sources independently corroborate as a structurally embedded, compulsory part of its curriculum; each has a clear organising logic (deepening one of two genuinely distinct professional/disciplinary emphases the comparator's own curriculum already names); each is substantively distinct, replacing at least 9 of the closest match's 24 courses (at least 67.5 EC) with UCR's own deeper data-science/media or entrepreneurship/business offerings, materially changing the alternative's academic priorities; and each is mechanically feasible against the enriched course database, with at least six distinct level-300 courses and pairwise differences of at least 9 courses (67.5 EC) against the closest match and 12 courses (90 EC) against each other, comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course floor. Production therefore includes both as the second and third alternatives. No generator-eligible evidence remains unassigned after the closest match and these two candidates together account for all nineteen generator-eligible rows, so production includes the maximum of three alternatives and records 'maximum-reached' as the stopping state.

notes.text: All three UCR alternatives include substantial study of the comparator's shared sociological-theory and methods core. The comparator additionally includes specialist components -- social-network and social-media analysis, co-creative/participatory research, education/labour-market/income inequality, health-and-welfare-state inequality, a second restricted gender-inequality elective, and a dedicated post-project impact-evaluation course (Onderzoek naar effecten van interventies) -- that UCR does not offer at the same level of depth or in dedicated form; UCR students can instead combine adjacent data-science, qualitative-methods, social-movements or public-economics coursework, but those specialist components are not reproduced.

VU organises applied professional practice around four compulsory, sequentially structured 6-EC project courses (Beleidsinterventie, Opdrachtonderzoek, Sociaal ondernemerschap, Consultancy), each pairing sociological content with a named professional role and an external societal partner. At UCR, comparable applied skills are distributed across separate courses in economics, law, negotiation, entrepreneurship, marketing and strategy rather than organised as credited partner-facing projects; the UCR alternatives therefore approach the same professional territory through a different curricular structure rather than reproducing the comparator's own project-course format.
